scope: Bounded primary-literature rereading for the scientific opening and synthesis. This is not an exhaustive novelty search or independent audit of every cited proof.

primary_sources.publication: A.S.Lewis and M.L.Overton, Mathematical Programming141 (2013),135–163, DOI10.1007/s10107-012-0514-2.
primary_sources.fresh_read: Introduction, Algorithm2.1, Algorithm4.6, Section5.1 qualification, and full text of Challenge7.1 on printedp160/PDFpage26.
claim_locators: Introduction printedpp136–139: nonsmooth experiments, jump secants and ill-conditioned inverse matrices.
Section2: full update and breakdown/smooth-stationary termination distinctions.

challenge_assumptions.objective: locally Lipschitz and semialgebraic, with bounded sublevel sets; convexity not required
challenge_assumptions.algorithm: Algorithm2.1 with BFGS update(2.2), Algorithm4.6 and any fixed0<c1<c2<1
challenge_assumptions.initialization: Absolutely continuous initial-data laws; the concrete example samples x0 normally and H0 from a Wishart law.
challenge_assumptions.quantifier: The four proposed properties are asked to hold with probability one.

challenge_items.1: Neither theoretical breakdown at a nondifferentiable accepted iterate nor termination at a smooth stationary point.
challenge_items.2: Every cluster point is Clarke stationary.
challenge_items.3: All function trial values converge R-linearly to the cluster-point value. This is stronger than convergence of accepted values alone.
challenge_items.4: If iterates converge to a partly smooth point relative to a manifold, the subspaces generated by eigenvectors whose eigenvalues vanish converge to its V-space (equivalently complementary U-space).

primary_sources.important_scope_difference: Our successful zero-gradient termination convention differs from Challenge item1. Our theorem assertions concern infinite admissible runs; deterministic exceptional starts give no positive-probability statement. No claim that the full challenge is refuted or resolved.
primary_sources.access_limit: PDF screenshot endpoint failed, but the complete challenge and surrounding text were obtained from the primary PDF text layer. No source PDF was saved in the repository.

primary_sources.publication: J.Guo and A.S.Lewis, SIAM Journal on Optimization28(2) (2018),1301–1311, DOI10.1137/17M1121883.
primary_sources.version: 11-page author manuscript with published title; numbering used here differs from the2017 preprint.
primary_sources.fresh_read: Definition2.1; Powell Theorem3.1 and extension theorem3.2; Theorems4.1/4.3, Corollaries4.2/4.4 and the explicit open-conjecture paragraph. Relevant proof arguments read; not an audit of every external dependency.

common_assumptions.sequence: Full inverse BFGS; arbitrary SPD initialization; fixed 0<c1<c2<1; differentiable accepted iterates with nonzero gradients; positive Armijo–weak-Wolfe steps. This matches Guo–Lewis Definition2.1 for infinite sequences.
common_assumptions.domain: Open convex U containing the sequence, finite convex f:U→R, compact initial sublevel withinU.
common_assumptions.base_conclusion: Objective values approach min f. Additional uniqueness converts value convergence on a compact sublevel to whole-iterate convergence.

3.2.condition: An open V⊂U contains closure of the entire iterate sequence; inf_V f=min f; Hessian is continuous and positive definite throughoutV.
3.2.technique: Smooth convex extension on a compact region preserving the relevant function values/gradients, followed by Powell.

4.1.condition: For everyδ>0 there is C² convex fδ on an open convex neighborhood Uδ⊂U of the initial sublevel, agreeing with f whenever f(x0)≥f(x)≥min f+δ.
4.1.technique: Contradiction assumes a positive limiting gap, so the same BFGS sequence is also a sequence for the smooth replacement.

4.3.condition: An open V⊂U contains closure of the sequence and has inf_V f=min f; for everyδ>0, a C² convex replacement on an open convex neighborhood of the initial sublevel agrees wherever dist(x,Vᶜ)>δ.
4.3.technique: Replacement away from a shrinking nonsmooth neighborhood, followed by approximation of the infimum throughV.

4.2.conclusion: Every BFGS sequence converges to0 in arbitrary finite dimension.

4.4.locator: Corollary4.4 and immediately following paragraph, printedp9/PDFpage9
4.4.conclusion: A subsequence approaches a point on v=0; the following paragraph explicitly leaves all-sequence convergence to(0,0) open.
4.4.proof_role: If closure avoided v=0, the smooth-replacement theorem would force convergence to zero, a contradiction.

primary_sources.comparison: The manuscript now credits the general extension framework and the norm result, then identifies the specific stronger mixed-benchmark conclusion. It does not describe all Guo–Lewis results as behavior-assumption theorems.
primary_sources.access_limit: The author manuscript is the freshly inspected version. No third-party paper bytes are redistributed.

primary_sources.version: Explicitv1 text; no journal publication is asserted.
primary_sources.fresh_read: SectionII objective/update/AssumptionII.1 and termination convention; TheoremII.1; TheoremIV.1 and related escape explanation.
primary_sources.model: f(x)=|x1|+Σ_{i=2}^n xi, n≥2. Invertible coordinate equivalence covers |v1ᵀx|+v2ᵀx for linearly independentv1,v2.
primary_sources.algorithm_assumptions: Full inverse BFGS; arbitrary SPD initialization; fixed 0<c1<c2<1; differentiable accepted iterates with nonzero gradients; positive Armijo–weak-Wolfe steps. This matches Guo–Lewis Definition2.1 for infinite sequences.
primary_sources.extra_convention: The source calls the algorithm terminated when no Armijo–Wolfe acceptable step exists. The impossibility is due to curvature; the direction is then unbounded below.
primary_sources.theorem_locator: TheoremIV.1, under AssumptionII.1 (differentiable iterates); TheoremII.1 gives affine invariance.
primary_sources.conclusion: After finitely many accepted BFGS iterations an unbounded descent direction is exposed. Typical expanding trial searches drive values to−∞; the theorem does not bound the number of evaluations needed to finish that unbounded search.
primary_sources.comparison: Our compact/coercive homogeneous results concern minimization and larger homogeneous classes. Companion infinite-run value alternatives do not supersede finite escape on this two-piece model.
primary_sources.access_limit: Fresh primary arXivHTML read; no downloaded source copy.

primary_sources.publication: B.Gebken, Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications209, article57 (8May2026), DOI10.1007/s10957-026-03008-z.
primary_sources.version: Published SpringerHTML. PublishedTheorem3.1 andLemma3.5 are not the preprint main-theorem number3.10.
primary_sources.fresh_read: Published introduction including the mixed benchmark, A1, the definition of N, all fiveB1 clauses, A2, Lemma3.5 and Theorem3.1 with proof.
primary_sources.benchmark_locator: Introduction paragraph beginning with the existing unbounded-below piecewise-linear results; it identifies x1²+|x2| convergence as not yet understood.
primary_sources.A1: f is a continuous selection of finitely many C¹ functions whose gradients are locally Lipschitz; convexity is not required by this objective class.

A2.A2.1: At a critical pointx*, gradients of all selection functions are affinely independent and have a zero linear combination with all coefficients strictly positive (these coefficients may be normalized to sum1).
A2.A2.2: x* is the unique global minimizer and there is z≠x* whose sublevel is bounded.

B1.B1.1: The run is infinite, has no breakdown, and every accepted gradient is nonzero.
B1.B1.2: The entire iterate sequence converges to xbar.
B1.B1.3: Each selection occurs infinitely often as an accepted gradient (membership in Ig(xk)).
B1.B1.4: Fixed positive σℓ,σu bound λj^k∈[σℓ,σu] for every k and every j=dimN(xbar)+1,…,n.

primary_sources.conclusion: UnderA2 there is a neighborhoodU ofx* such that a run starting inU and satisfyingB1 has a Clarke-critical limit.
primary_sources.comparison: Our convex objective-family theorems derive convergence without those iterate/spectral premises. Gebken treats a different, potentially nonconvex selection class and general quasi-Newton iteration; no theorem-wide domination is claimed.
primary_sources.access_limit: Fresh published primary text and relevant proof read; no source copies saved.
